clue.text: Marsupial primarily found in island, a native running wild

definitions.text: Marsupial primarily found in island, a native running wild

indicators.note: letters running wild are scattered out of order, so this pool is rearranged
primarily picks out only the opening letter of the word Marsupial

parts.note: first letter of Marsupial

explanation.surface: A description of a wild native animal of an island, as in a nature guide.
explanation.walkthrough: M (Marsupial's first letter) plus ISLANDANATIVE is rearranged by 'running wild'. The whole clue also defines the beast: a marsupial found only on the island of Tasmania, native and wild.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tasmanian devil is a carnivorous pouched mammal living wild only on Tasmania, an island state of Australia.

clue.text: Knowing what others have in mind, yet putting one's foot down

definitions.text: Knowing what others have in mind

parts.note: yet and though can both mean nevertheless
treading is putting one's foot down, step by step

explanation.surface: Someone who can sense others' thoughts yet still insists on having their own way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting one's foot down' suggests being firm, but here it is read literally as walking.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought-reading is telepathy, perceiving another person's unspoken thoughts.

clue.text: Diabolical and awful act, a sin

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly done, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A terrible act described as both diabolical and sinful.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanic describes something of the Devil, hence wicked or devilish.

clue.text: Section of Battersea Bridge men tackled as contracted work

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Workmen tackling a stretch of a London bridge as a job done under contract.
explanation.walkthrough: Battersea Bridge is a real bridge over the Thames in London, which makes the surface sound like a building job.
explanation.definitionFit: An abridgement is a shortened version of a book or other work, so a work that has been condensed.

clue.text: Rascally Irish taking politician for ring-leader

indicators.note: taking says a new piece is brought in to the word
for says the new piece stands in place of the old one

parts.note: taken as written
the leading letter of ring
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An Irish politician who led a ring of rogues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring-leader' looks like a gang boss but just means the first letter of ring; swap that R in IRISH for MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Impish means mischievous in the manner of a little imp or naughty child.

clue.text: Head male, accepted by rest as one with special status

parts.note: nob is slang for the head

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside the word that follows

parts.note: to lean is to rest against something

explanation.surface: A senior male figure welcomed by the others as someone special.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobleman holds a title of rank, a privileged position among the aristocracy.

clue.text: Priest repeatedly in the limelight

indicators.note: repeatedly in says the word sits inside these words, and more than once

explanation.surface: A clergyman who is always in the public eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters appear twice: across 'thE LImelight' and again inside 'limELIght'. Eli is the priest at Shiloh who raised Samuel in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Eli is the Old Testament priest of Shiloh, a crossword regular among biblical clerics.

clue.text: In which characters are inclined to show stress

definitions.text: In which characters are inclined to show stress

parts.words: In which characters are inclined to show stress
parts.note: characters are letters of type, and inclined means sloping, used for emphasis

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like people disposed to display anxiety; really it is printed letters leaning sideways for emphasis.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type slopes to the right and is used to emphasise words in printed text.

clue.text: Listing an elite, unusually bright people

indicators.note: unusually says these letters appear in an uncommon arrangement

explanation.surface: Drawing up a list of a select, exceptionally clever group.
explanation.definitionFit: The intelligentsia are the intellectual class, clever and educated people collectively.

clue.text: It appears, on the surface, to get court involved in a little work

indicators.note: in says the mixed letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Something seems superficially to drag a law court into a minor job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the surface' reads as 'seemingly' but is literal: the rock shows at ground level.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is a rock formation that shows above the ground, exposed where it breaks the soil.

clue.text: Keep it in mind, it's what we live on

indicators.note: Keep says one piece holds another
in shows which piece goes inside the other

parts.note: brain and mind are used interchangeably for one's intellect

explanation.surface: Advice to remember something, followed by the reason, as if it were our livelihood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What we live on' sounds like money or food; it is the island the setter's readers live on.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Britain is the island home of the British readers of this Sunday paper.

clue.text: Military leader's limited intelligence

indicators.note: limited means cut short, so only the opening part is kept

parts.note: a general is a senior army commander

explanation.surface: A jibe that an army commander is not very bright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limited intelligence' looks like an insult but 'limited' trims GENERAL to its start, and 'intelligence' means information.
explanation.definitionFit: Gen is informal British slang for information, as in military intelligence.

clue.text: It could be okay after last of sweet

definitions.text: It could be okay after last of sweet

parts.words: It could be okay after last of sweet
parts.note: the final letter of sweet placed before okay spells a Hungarian wine, served with the pudding

explanation.surface: A suggestion that something might be acceptable once the sweets run out.
explanation.walkthrough: T (last of sweet) then OKAY gives TOKAY, a sweet Hungarian wine; the answer is the category it is an example of.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokay is a rich sweet wine from Hungary, an example of the kind served with pudding.

clue.text: Computer problem that brought an end to investment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: malicious software disguised as something harmless

definitions.text: that brought an end to investment
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the wooden horse that ended the Greek siege of Troy, investment meaning siege

explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment' looks financial but is the old military sense of besieging a town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greeks hid soldiers in a wooden horse to enter Troy; modern malware borrows the name for hidden harmful code.

clue.text: Exactly the right thing, a collector's item

definitions.meaning: first meaning: 'just the ...' is the ideal thing
second meaning: what a ... collector takes from passengers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Collector's item' suggests an antique; it is what a ticket inspector collects.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'just the ticket' means exactly what is needed, and a ticket collector gathers passes.

clue.text: Celebrate first piece of luggage appearing here?

definitions.text: Celebrate first piece of luggage appearing here?

parts.note: to carouse is to drink and celebrate noisily

indicators.note: first piece of picks only the opening letter of luggage

parts.note: first letter of luggage

explanation.surface: A traveller cheering as their first bag arrives at the airport reclaim belt.
explanation.definitionFit: At an airport baggage hall, suitcases come round on a rotating conveyor belt.

clue.text: A term of Latin that follows some examples

definitions.text: A term of Latin that follows some examples

parts.words: A term of Latin that follows some examples
parts.note: a Latin phrase written at the end of a short list to mean and the rest

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a grammar lesson; the phrase is the one added after listing a few examples.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means 'and the rest', used to close an incomplete list.

clue.text: Request admission, wanting to dine inside

indicators.note: inside says one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: entry means admission, being let in
to eat is to dine

explanation.surface: Asking to be let into a restaurant because one wants to eat there.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest plea or appeal to someone.

clue.text: Obediently follow instructions, say, pulling rope

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to toe the line is to obey, giving toe line

explanation.surface: Doing as one is told, for instance when hauling on a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'toe the line' is to conform; TOE LINE spoken aloud matches a rope for towing.
explanation.definitionFit: A towline is a rope or cable used to haul a vehicle or boat behind another.

clue.text: European pest could be annoying

parts.note: may expresses possibility, what could be
to bug someone is to annoy them

explanation.surface: A warning that a pest found in Europe might be a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: The maybug, or cockchafer, is a European beetle whose grubs damage crops and roots.

clue.text: Children at home absorbed by Disney classic

indicators.note: absorbed by says one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: Bambi is the 1942 Disney film about a young deer
in means at home

explanation.surface: Kids sitting at home engrossed in an old Disney film.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambini is Italian for little children or babies, used informally in English.

clue.text: Scene of conflict for Russians starting Dostoevsky's novel

indicators.note: starting means only the opening stretch of the title is used

parts.note: Crime and Punishment is Dostoevsky's best-known novel

explanation.surface: A battleground for Russians beginning to read a Russian classic.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening six letters of CRIME AND PUNISHMENT run across the gap between the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimean peninsula was the battleground of the 1850s Crimean War and the scene of later fighting.

clue.text: Realistic, having been affected by gravity of our situation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: practical, sensible and unpretentious

definitions.text: having been affected by gravity of our situation
definitions.meaning: second meaning: pulled by our planet's gravity, so fallen to the ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gravity of our situation' sounds like seriousness; it is the literal pull of the planet we stand on.
explanation.definitionFit: A down-to-earth person is practical and sensible; something falling is drawn to the ground.

clue.text: Island, despite what Donne said

parts.note: the poet John Donne wrote 'No ... is an island' in a 1624 meditation, yet one island bears that very word

explanation.walkthrough: Donne's line 'No man is an island' is contradicted by the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is a self-governing island between Great Britain and Ireland.

clue.text: Humming sound, including mystic syllable

indicators.note: including says one piece contains the other

parts.note: a noise is a sound
om is the sacred syllable chanted in Hindu and Buddhist meditation

explanation.surface: A meditative hum with a sacred chant inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humming' looks like a sound but is slang for smelling bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Humming is British slang for stinking, and noisome means foul-smelling or offensive.

clue.text: Poet's frequently using old paper

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A poet who often writes on old paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Oft is the archaic or poetic form of often.

clue.text: Space for comment — add excessive amounts of it?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the blank edges of a page where notes are written
second meaning, read as two words: to spoil a gin and it (gin with Italian vermouth) by pouring in too much it

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as MAR GINS: overdoing the 'it' in a gin and it would spoil the drinks. 'It' is Italian vermouth here.
explanation.definitionFit: Margins are the blank borders round printed text, used for writing annotations.

clue.text: Wrongly incarcerate over strike in Western region

indicators.note: wrongly says these letters are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

parts.note: to lam is to hit or thrash

explanation.surface: An unjust imprisonment over a labour strike somewhere in the West.
explanation.definitionFit: The isthmus linking North and South America lies in the Western Hemisphere.
